name: Automate deprovisioning from the HR system of record
description: Make termination in the HR system the trigger for access removal, so revocation is a deterministic system event with a measurable timestamp rather than a coordinated manual task.
responsible_role: IT / Identity and Access Management owner

steps.action: Establish the HR system as the authoritative source for employment status, including contractors.
Integrate the HR system with the identity provider so termination automatically disables the identity and revokes active sessions and tokens.
Map downstream applications to identity provider lifecycle events, and enumerate any application that cannot be integrated.
Define a documented manual path with the same committed timeframe for applications that cannot be integrated.
Instrument the elapsed time between termination and revocation so adherence is measurable rather than asserted.
Set the committed timeframe in the access control policy to a value the automated process reliably achieves.

implementation_considerations: The HR-to-identity-provider link is usually the easy part; the schedule is set by how many downstream applications cannot consume lifecycle events.
Contractors are frequently absent from the HR system entirely. Resolve where contractor status is authoritative before building on it.
Set the committed timeframe after measuring what the automation actually achieves, not before.
typical_duration: Weeks, dominated by application integration rather than the HR-to-IdP link itself.
prerequisites: An HR system that reliably records terminations promptly
An identity provider that is genuinely authoritative for the applications in scope

verification_method.how: Sample terminations after the change and compare HR termination timestamps to identity provider revocation timestamps and downstream entitlement state. Confirm the measured interval is within the committed timeframe.

residual_risk_note: Applications outside the identity provider retain a manual dependency and remain the most likely source of future overruns. Track them as a named exception list rather than assuming coverage.
period_limitation_note: Automating deprovisioning does not remove an overrun that already occurred during an elapsed examination period. The exception will be reported; this remediation reduces recurrence and supports management's response.
notes: Automation is one way to meet the objective, not a required control. A reliably operated manual process with measurable timestamps can be equally acceptable.
